correctness.rationale: The exact conditional Gaussian Schur complement follows from the free-flight covariances \(\operatorname{Var}(X_t)=2Dt^3/3\), \(\operatorname{Cov}(X_t,V_t)=Dt^2\), and \(\operatorname{Var}(V_t)=2Dt\). Conditioning the exponential backward age gives an exact posterior proportional to \(t^{-3/2}\exp[-rt-3x^2/(4Dt^3)]\). The unique saddle \(\tau_x=(9x^2/(4Dr))^{1/4}\) yields \(\varphi(z)=z+1/(3z^3)\), with a strict minimum \(4/3\) at \(z=1\) and second derivative \(4\). The oriented joint density has exponent \(\Psi(z,u)=\varphi(z)+(u-1/z)^2/z\) and a polynomial prefactor; coercivity provides a full good LDP. Under the non-outward constraint \(u\le0\), the minimum is \(u=0,z=\sqrt2\), producing \(4(\sqrt2-1)/3\). The open-event limit agrees by approaching the boundary from below. An independent conditional standard Gaussian gives \(B=-\sigma A+Z/\sqrt2+o_{\Pr}(1)\), with \(A\sim\mathcal N(0,1/4)\); covariance and second moments follow using uniform Laplace moment bounds. A standalone standard-library checker replayed the rational Gaussian covariance, rate, local curvature, conditional moment quadrature, and wrong-way tail at two large parameters. Finite tests supplement the analytic proofs.

originality.rationale: The exact complete-reset joint Gaussian–exponential stationary mixture and its stretched-exponential position tail were already derived in Singh (2020). The inspected pertinent source does not state the far-position conditioned *velocity* full LDP, exact wrong-way exponent, or coupled age–velocity Gaussian law. The two further source comparisons involve crossing-weighted rather than snapshot velocities and velocity-only rather than complete resetting. Research-index searches found neighboring age saddle and velocity facts in different models, but no identical or dominating conditional theorem. The nonroutine conditional speed, wrong-direction penalty, and joint fluctuation profile remain meaningful asymptotic consequences not stated in the compared literature; implicit derivability from a published exact joint density remains a substantive priority risk.

value.rationale: The stationary randomly accelerated resetting system is a natural exactly solvable inertial-transport model. Conditioning on a rare remote position probes whether particles are still moving away or are returning, an observable not captured by the marginal spatial tail alone. The full velocity rate profile, exact non-outward penalty and correlated local age–velocity fluctuations give a structural, parameter-normalized rare-event description and distinguish stationary snapshots from flux-weighted crossings. The exact wrong-way exponent and correlation are not arbitrary slices, and the result allows independent numerical or physical tests. Its scope and priority risks are explicit.
